incidents.name: dForce iToken Curve read-only reentrancy
incidents.notes: The dForce wstETHCRV-gauge iToken priced its collateral from the Curve pool's get_virtual_price, which can be read mid-remove_liquidity, so re-entering from the pool's native-token refund let the attacker liquidate positions against a distorted valuation.

sources.ref: onchain review: iToken 0x2cE498b79C499c6BB64934042eBA487bD31F75ea created 2023-02-07T10:10:30Z by 0xde6d6f23aabbdc9469c8907ece7c379f98e4cb75, not the attack-tx sender 0xe0d551017c0111ac11108641771897aa33b2817c; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events between creation and the incident, so the executing code was 2.54 days old. Loss ~$3.6M as previously recorded. Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is an EIP-1967 proxy; its implementation slot holds 0x45b5636b01091336f02194d327374924d54a0772 at both the creation block 58760469 and the incident block 59527634, with a binary search of eth_getStorageAt over that range finding no intermediate write, the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks, and the implementation contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the executing code dates from deployment.

incidents.name: Lendf.Me (imBTC ERC-777 reentrancy)
incidents.notes: MoneyMarket.supply() credited the supplier only after doTransferIn(), so imBTC's ERC-777 tokensToSend hook re-entered withdraw() while the deposit was still counted, letting the attacker keep both the collateral credit and the withdrawn tokens.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0x0eee3e38 is the verified non-proxy MoneyMarket contract (EIP-1967 impl slot empty), created 2019-08-06 by 0xd30076b706fa0425bc52d0739224fe8ef1ae7c81, not by attack sender 0xa9bf70a4; DeFiHackLabs PoC src/test/2020-04/LendfMe_exp.sol reproduces the reentrant withdraw
